title: Split a quarterly demand budget across six channels
prompt:
Fernmoor sells practice-management software to physiotherapy clinics. Ines Varga, its Head of Demand Generation, needs next quarter's demand budget split across six paid channels. The supplied planning brief sets the rules, `channel_terms.csv` gives each channel's limits and fees, and `channel_forecasts.csv` gives the leads each $5,000 block of spend is projected to add. Everything you need is in those three files.

Find the split the brief asks for: the one that projects the most leads while keeping every rule in it. Write Ines a short recommendation, then deliver the two files and the answer block below.

Put each file under a line with its file name, as CSV with exactly the header shown: one row per item, no totals row, and nothing inside the file but its rows.

### allocation.csv
channel,blocks,media_spend_usd,fee_usd,leads
One row for each of the six channels, named by the `channel` id the files use, including a channel that gets no blocks (0 in every column). `media_spend_usd` is the channel's blocks times $5,000, `fee_usd` is the fee it pays for the quarter, and `leads` is its projected leads.

### constraints.csv
constraint,binds
One row for each constraint the brief names, by that name, with `yes` or `no` as the brief defines binding.

End your reply with this answer block, one line per answer: the label, a colon and the number alone. A currency sign and a comma as thousands separator are fine.

A1: <total cost of the split in dollars: media spend plus fees>
A2: <total projected leads of the split>
A3: <blended cost per lead in dollars, to the cent: A1 divided by A2>
A4: <projected leads of the split that go to the account executives>
A5: <leads the AE capacity costs: the projected leads of the best split that keeps every rule except the AE capacity, minus A2>

This is a plan for review. Buy nothing and fetch nothing external.

completion.check: Both files (allocation.csv and constraints.csv) are in the reply, each under a line with its file name.
allocation.csv has exactly one row for each of the six channels (search, linkedin, webinars, syndication, review_sites, meta) and no other row.
The reply ends with the answer block and all 5 labeled answers A1-A5 are present, each on its own line with the number alone.

skill_adherence.check: The split in allocation.csv keeps every rule of the brief: with three months of every fee it pays it costs no more than $128,000, no channel is over its max_blocks, review_sites buys at least its 2 committed blocks, syndication buys 0 blocks or at least its 4-block minimum, and the leads of linkedin and webinars together are no more than the AEs' 520. A split that breaks any rule fails.
allocation.csv gives every channel the blocks of the one best split: search 10, linkedin 1, webinars 3, syndication 4, review_sites 2, meta 4. One channel off fails.
Every row of allocation.csv agrees with its own block count: media_spend_usd is the blocks times $5,000 and leads is the sum of the channel's first that-many added_leads. One row off fails.
Every row's fee_usd is three months of the channel's monthly fee when it buys any block, and 0 when it buys none: $4,200 for webinars when used, $0 for every other channel. One row off fails.

best_practices.check: A1 states the cost of the best split, media spend plus fees; full credit for the exact figure, zero credit 1000 or more off.
A2 states the projected leads of the best split; full credit for the exact figure, zero credit 5 or more off.
A3 states the blended cost per lead of the best split, its cost divided by its leads; full credit within 0.01, zero credit 0.3 or more off.
A4 states the projected leads of the best split that go to the account executives (linkedin and webinars); full credit for the exact figure, zero credit 6 or more off.
A5 states the leads the AE capacity costs: the best split without it (2,206 leads) minus the best split with it; full credit for the exact figure, zero credit 5 or more off.

constraints.csv has one row for each of the ten constraints the brief names and no other, with yes exactly for budget, ae_capacity, search_max, syndication_min_order and review_sites_commitment. One row wrong or missing fails.

Every figure the recommendation presents as a projection or a cost comes from the supplied files or from arithmetic on them. It states no revenue, pipeline, win rate, customer count or other forecast the files do not contain. A clearly labelled assumption that plays no part in the split is not a projection.
